level-1.title: Money can grow in different places
summary: Money in a box stays the same. Money in a bank grows a little.
There are other places money can go where it may grow more.
But those places can also go down. Some months your money is worth less.
Safe places grow slowly and never fall. Risky places may grow fast or fall.
Nobody can promise you what will happen. Anyone who promises is not telling the truth.

level-2.title: What a mutual fund actually is
summary: A mutual fund pools money from many people. A manager buys shares in many companies with it.
You own a small slice of the whole pool, so one company doing badly does not sink you.
A SIP puts a fixed amount in every month — ₹500, say — instead of one lump sum.
A bank deposit or PPF promises you a number. A mutual fund promises nothing at all.
That is the whole difference. Higher possible growth is paid for with the chance of going down.
Money you need soon should not go in a fund. Money you will not touch for years might.

image.alt: Many hands putting coins into one pot

options.label: Many people's money pooled and invested together
A special kind of bank account

questions.hint: The word 'mutual' is the clue. It is shared.

level-3.title: Risk, time and a fund in your own name
summary: Every place for money trades three things: how much it might grow, how likely you are to lose some, and how fast you can get it back.
A savings account is instant and safe at about 4%. PPF is locked for years at about 7%. A fund could beat both, or lose money — nothing is promised.
Since prices rise around 6% a year, money sitting at 4% is quietly shrinking in what it can buy. Safety is not free either.
A SIP of ₹500 a month is ₹6,000 a year. Its value is whatever the units are worth on the day you sell, which may be more or less than you paid.
A minor can hold a fund. The child is the sole owner and an adult only operates it — no joint holding is allowed.
Two traps worth knowing: the folio FREEZES on your eighteenth birthday until you convert it yourself, and money taken out is paid only into a bank account in your own name.
So the account comes first, the emergency savings come second, and the fund comes third. In that order, never reversed.
